Anya: quick sync — ACME trial asked if we can commit to a 99th-percentile latency SLA for hosted text-gen: target sub-500ms p99 for short prompts. We need to pick priorities: adaptive batching, KV-prefetch, or 4-bit quant kernels?

Sam: do we have p99 baselines for their workload? they said avg prompt ~20 tokens and bursty concurrency.

Diego: baseline from latest perf run:
```
model: redwood-7b-v1
p50: 120ms
p95: 230ms
p99: 610ms
throughput: 400 req/s per GPU
cost/tok: $0.0008
```

Katie: 610ms p99 is above their ask. Short list of levers: batching (better throughput, risk for single-request tail), KV-prefix caching (helps chat sessions), quant+kernel opt (lower per-token latency).

Ben: ops note — batching needs explicit SLOs. It can worsen tails at low QPS if we wait for batches. Also quant kernels can introduce subtle accuracy/errors we must vet.

Sam: quick RICE sketch (very rough):
```
Feature    Reach Impact Confidence Effort RICE
Batching     60%   6      70%        3     84
KV-cache     30%   7      80%        2     84
Quant-4bit   90%   5      40%        5     36
```
(Reach = percent of ACME-like workloads helped)

Diego: those numbers show KV is great for chat but ACME is bursty short prompts — batching + kernel opt might give quicker wins for them.

Anya: launch criteria to propose: p99 < 500ms on ACME workload, error rate increase <= 5% vs baseline, and no >15% regression in throughput or cost per token.

Katie: sequencing proposal across 3 sprints — Sprint 1: lightweight adaptive batching (opt-in per route); Sprint 2: KV-prefetch for chat routes; Sprint 3: canary 4-bit kernels with perf vetting.

Ben: add canary requirements: automatic rollback if errors >3% absolute increase or p50 regresses >50ms. Also wire cost monitoring for canary.

Sam: dev+infra+qa effort estimates: batching 2.5 engineer-sprints, KV 2 eng-sprints, quant 4 eng-sprints (includes kernel vetting and accuracy tests).

Anya: tradeoff: batching first to hit SLA faster, but KV is lower-risk for per-request tail. I lean batching + strict canary gates.

Diego: +1 to batching first, but require per-route config and an opt-out flag for single-shot low-latency customers.

Katie: CS notes — ACME will accept staged improvements weekly during peak hours if we can show steady p99 reduction. Their priority is p99 during spikes.

Ben: I'll draft SLO rubric and canary playbook with rollback thresholds and thresholds for cost regressions.

Anya: action items:
- Sam: run final perf experiments for adaptive batching by EOD Thu
- Diego: prototype per-route KV cache metrics + feature flag by Mon
- Ben: canary + rollback doc by Tue
- Katie: coordinate ACME expectation email draft

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: perf-canary-1 -> us-west at 2025-04-22T09:00:00Z :construction:

Sam: ack — will post experiment results here.
